title: Claude Cowork
content:
## Overview

**Claude Cowork** is Anthropic's product for handing Claude open-ended, multi-step work that runs asynchronously rather than in a single back-and-forth chat turn. In July 2026, Anthropic expanded Cowork from a desktop-only feature to **mobile and web**, letting sessions and files follow a user across devices.

---

## Platform Availability

Cowork is now accessible through:

- The Claude app on **iPhone, iPad, and Android**
- **claude.ai** in the browser
- Desktop (original surface)

The cross-platform rollout began in beta for Max subscribers, with Anthropic stating it would extend to other paid plans in the following weeks.

---

## Background Work & Scheduled Tasks

The core capability is that work keeps running without a device needing to stay online:

- **Scheduled cloud-based tasks** run on a cadence the user defines (daily, weekly, custom) with no device needing to be online at trigger time — this is the same underlying mechanism used by scheduled prompts in Claude Code.
- Users can start a task at a desk, check progress from a phone, and pick up the finished output from wherever is convenient.
- **Mobile push notifications** surface when Claude needs human judgment or explicit permission before continuing — for example, before submitting a form, sending an email, or taking an action with real-world side effects — keeping a human in the loop before anything irreversible happens.

---

## Cross-Device Workflow

Because sessions and files sync across devices, a typical flow looks like:

1. Kick off a research or drafting task from the desktop app
2. Get a mobile notification when Claude needs a decision or hits a permission gate
3. Approve or redirect from the phone
4. Return to desktop (or stay on mobile) to review the finished output

This mirrors the pattern used by scheduled Claude Code tasks (see the Claude Code Overview page) but is aimed at general knowledge work rather than software engineering specifically.

---

## Usage Patterns (from Anthropic's released data)

Anthropic published anonymized usage data covering **1.2 million Cowork sessions across roughly 600,000 organizations**:

- **Over 90% of usage was non-coding work.**
- **Business operations and content creation** together accounted for nearly half of all Cowork activity.

This is a notable contrast with Claude Code, whose usage is overwhelmingly software-engineering-focused — Cowork is positioned as the general-purpose "agentic assistant for knowledge work" surface, while Claude Code remains the specialized coding agent.

---

## Why It Matters

Cowork's mobile/web expansion signals Anthropic's push to make asynchronous, permission-gated agentic work a mainstream product pattern beyond developers — the same scheduled-task-plus-approval-gate model that has proven useful for Claude Code repository maintenance (like this wiki's own agent) is now the default way non-technical users are expected to delegate work to Claude.
